reviews.core_assessment:
Independently read every selected context and proof range74-112,170-280,286-613,650-1142,1185-1427 before viewing the selector difficulty reason. The property-P proof passes from a finite translation-stable field extension to a finite map of smooth curves. A finite branch locus invariant under a nontorsion translation is empty; Riemann-Hurwitz and the elliptic morphism classification reduce the extension to a sublattice cover. Its normality then identifies the embedded extension inside the union K. Tsen supplies C1 for the directed union, not the nontrivial no-finite-translation-extension conclusion.
The Riccati classification is verified by the actual gauge matrices and their antidiagonal equations. In the scalar case the ratio sigma(u)/u is a phi-coboundary. Its norm is phi-invariant and hence constant, so a constant root normalizes it to norm1 and Hilbert90 supplies m. The resulting scalar coefficient descends; the remaining finite cyclic constant matrix representation diagonalizes, giving two invariant row ratios. The two-step descent first uses M_(kLambda)/M_(Z+k tau Z), and if necessary obtains three tau-translates, scalarizes over that intermediate field, and descends again. Distinctness is maintained by invertibility of the matrices.
The theta-gcd construction removes the common shifted numerator/denominator factor r. Substitution into the Riccati equation and the two coprimeness conditions force divisor bounds p<=p2 and q<=phi^-1(p3). Quasiperiodicity then forces equal degrees and the weight relation weight(p/q)=deg(r)h modulo kLambda. The corrected /k multiplier is actually printed at1126 and1134, so the operative proof uses the correct formula despite550.
For irreducibility, the lifted zero/pole support of b on C/(2Lambda) restricts weight(p/q) to ell z0-deg(q)h modulo Lambda, with |ell|<=4. The stronger author group-intersection condition excludes nonzero multiples of h in these cosets, forcing deg(r)=deg(q)=deg(p)=0 and hence a constant Riccati solution, incompatible with nonconstant b.
For imprimitivity the second Riccati equation uses phi^2. The support bounds allow extra negative h shifts in the numerator and positive h shifts in the denominator; any such mass contributes a positive integer d to(2deg(r)+d)h=ell z0 modulo Lambda, with |ell|<=8. Nonresonance removes all these extra contributions and then deg(r). At each lattice pole the bracket is holomorphic, so u must have the full double pole there; equality of total degrees forces exactly the zero divisor of b as well. Thus u=cb. The pole at -2h forces c=-1/a, and the remaining equality is1=0. This is a separate argument, not a repetition of the first Riccati conclusion.
The determinant sentence is an abbreviated standard first-order PV/divisor check, assessed below. For the arithmetic step, wp(z0) algebraic implies the elliptic point and its integer multiples are algebraic. A relation m1 h=m2 z0+lambda either makes m1 h a period, forcing m1=0 by nontorsion, or gives an elliptic logarithm of a nonzero algebraic point; Schneider makes that logarithm transcendental, contrary to algebraic h and integer m1. This establishes the stronger group-intersection condition already explicitly stated by the author.

For propertyP, the finite translation-compatible extension gives an unramified cover of an elliptic curve because any finite branch-value set invariant under nontorsion translation is empty; Riemann-Hurwitz and elliptic-morphism classification put its function field back inside the covering-field union. In the cyclic descent, an entry of sigma(T)T^(-1) gives the scalar eigen-cocycle; its norm is constant, normalization gives norm1, Hilbert90 makes the transformed scalar invariant, and the remaining constant finite cyclic representation diagonalizes. Ratios of the two nonzero rows are fixed and distinct. The first descent is M_(kLambda) to M_(Z+k tau Z), and the second uses that intermediate field to M_Lambda; the rank-two cover is never incorrectly treated as one cyclic extension. The theta-gcd calculation uses the actual coprimality relations to force p|p2 and q|phi^(-1)p3, and the correct theta multiplier gives equal degrees and the weight constraint. In the generic calculation, nonresonance forces nonnegative degree sums to vanish. The imprimitive phi^2 equation requires a separate divisor inventory: every disallowed shifted zero/pole contributes a positive h coefficient, so the remaining numerator zeros lie above plus/minus z0 and denominator poles lie above0. issues.decision: The universal equality Zh intersect(ell*z0+Lambda)={0} cannot be literal for a coset not containing0. The counted arithmetic proof establishes the sufficient GROUP condition Zh intersect(Z*z0+Lambda)={0}. Every use of the generic proof only excludes a nonzero integer multiple ofh in the relevant coset. For theta_k(z)=theta(z/k), the multiplier is exp(2pi*i*omega/k). Degree-zero periodicity therefore requires the chosen representative omega in kZ. The original functional equation478 and the later correctly scaled displays1126/1134 uniquely determine this. The r002 note is sufficient and leaves the author text intact.

The curve cover goes from C/(aLambda-double-prime) to C/Lambda-prime, contravariantly to the field inclusion. In the general cyclic-descent lemma T-double-prime lies in M_(Lambda-double-prime); indexk alone does not imply the printed M_(kLambda). The actual two applications use the explicit fields shown in the source and satisfy the needed cyclic extension hypotheses. The current visible note correctly limits the claim.

The algebraicity of g2,g3,h,A,B is in the original Weierstrass coordinates. Scaling a period to1 can destroy algebraicity, but the generic analytic GL2 calculation only needs complex coefficients and its nonresonance condition is preserved by simultaneous scaling. Schneider is applied before this analytic normalization in the original coordinates. The r002 note makes this necessary separation explicit.

If the determinant image were finite, the allowed first-order PV criterion would give b^m=phi(f)/f with m>=1 and f in some M_(kLambda). On C/(kLambda), every translation-byh orbit has total divisor multiplicity0 for phi(f)/f. The orbit of0 contains exactly one of the lifted poles ofb and no lifted zero: any other pole would require nh inLambda, and a zero would require nh in plus/minus z0+Lambda, both excluded for n!=0. Its divisor sum for b^m is therefore-2m, a contradiction. This is the direct telescoping-divisor application already indicated by the author abbreviation; no replacement author proof is inserted.

boundary_checks.conclusion: The cyclic image in GL2(C) is finite, hence diagonalizable in characteristic0. The scalar gauge equation forces the two row denominators to be nonzero, and invertibility makes the two row ratios distinct. Cyclicity alone for an infinite representation would not suffice, but the source group here is finite.
p,q,r are entire theta products, so their degrees are nonnegative. This is essential when the arithmetic h coefficient is forced to0; an arbitrary meromorphic r would not permit that conclusion.

At every point ofLambda, the left bracket in1383 is regular: its possible poles are inLambda-h orLambda-2h. The right side has an exact double pole because b(h) is finite and nonzero; nonresonance excludes h congruent to plus/minus z0. The allowed denominator order is at most2, forcing equality at all four lifts modulo2Lambda. The subsequent pole at-2h cannot be cancelled by phi(b), forcing c=-1/a.

If z0 and-z0 coincide moduloLambda, the divisor formulas retain their multiplicities. The degree and weight bounds continue to apply; no assumption of two distinct simple zeros was silently introduced.

The standing non-torsion assumption1234 excludes h=0. In the relation m1*h=m2*z0+lambda, the algebraic elliptic point atz0 remains algebraic under multiplication. A period gives m1=0 by nontorsion; a nonperiod algebraic elliptic logarithm value contradicts Schneider since m1*h would be algebraic. The new theorem does not assume algebraicity of normalized periods.

Irreducible and primitive alone would not automatically rule out finite primitive subgroups. The source first proves propertyP and obtains the cyclic component quotient, then invokes the stated algebraic-subgroup classification to reduce to the determinant character. The proof retains that prerequisite chain.
